title: Per-SKU reservation lock and the new restock path use different locks
diff: +    # Two concurrent reservations for the same SKU used to be able to
+    # both read the same `available` before either wrote back,
+    # oversold. A per-SKU lock makes the read-check-write atomic for
+    """Called from the warehouse webhook when new inventory arrives.
+    Serialized against other restock webhooks with a single lock,

+- reserve_stock is now guarded by a per-SKU lock, closing a
+  read-modify-write race between two concurrent reservations for the
+- New restock_and_release_holds, called from the warehouse webhook
+  when inventory arrives, serialized against duplicate webhook

ground_truth.explanation: reserve_stock is correctly hardened with a per-SKU lock (_lock_for(sku)) so two concurrent reservations for the same SKU can no longer both read the same `available` before either writes back. The new restock_and_release_holds is guarded too, but by a single global _restock_lock meant only to serialize duplicate webhook deliveries against each other -- it does not acquire _lock_for(sku). Both functions still do read-then-write on the same _stock_cache[sku] entry, so a reservation and a restock for the same SKU can interleave: whichever write lands second silently clobbers the other's update, producing either oversold inventory or phantom stock. Each function looks correctly locked in isolation; the bug is that the two locks don't exclude each other.\n\nOffline validation (execution_validated): a standalone asyncio reproduction of both code paths, run 200 times with 6 concurrent reservations and 6 concurrent restocks racing against a starting stock of 5, showed the final stock count diverge from the arithmetically expected value in 182/200 trials (91%). A race not reproducing in N runs would not prove its absence; this reproduces readily.
ground_truth.validation_note: Standalone asyncio simulation of reserve_stock's per-SKU lock vs restock_and_release_holds' separate global lock, 200 trials of 6 concurrent reservations + 6 concurrent restocks: 182/200 (91.0%) showed a lost update. Script and raw output preserved as private provenance, not in this repository.
